Cricket Chokers

By: Julian Sun | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In the wake of yet another World Cup debacle, how will the Proteas pick up the pieces and shed that eternal tag of Chokers?

Unique Selling Point:
In the wake of a shock defeat to the Netherlands that dumped South Africa out of the T20 World Cup in Australia, we find out what's next for the shell-shocked Proteas and how South African cricket plans to move forward from yet another World Cup debacle.

Summary:
Since 1992, South Africa has endured many-a-painful exit from both the 50 over and T20 world Cups. Always full of promise, the Proteas have consistently flattered to deceive, earning the much-maligned "chokers" tag that they carry with ever-increasing weight around their necks.

Now in the wake of Sunday's shock loss to the lowly Netherlands, Temba Bavuma is the latest Captain to bear the burden of defeat. They return home with cricket in a state of flux. After years of maladministration that has seen hundreds of millions of rands in losses, the game in this country faces an existential threat. It comes at a time in which the very nature of world cricket is changing. As interest in bilateral series wanes, cricket boards from around the world are all turning to Domestic T20 leagues for financial salvation.



Further information:
India has the IPL, Australia the Big Bash, England the Hundred. And in January, South Africa will have the SA20.

This much-heralded T20 competition is the latest attempt by CSA to launch a successful domestic T20 league. Previous attempts have been unmitigated financial disasters. The Global T20 envisioned by former CEO Haroon Lorgat was canceled at the last minute, but not before CSA had invested millions into it. Its successor, the Mzansi Super League ran for 2 years, but failure to secure a broadcast sponsor resulted crippled it financially.

Headed by Commissioner Graeme Smith, the SA20 was launched in August. Scheduled for January and February 2023, the tournament will be played between 6 newly-formed franchises bankrolled by wealthy IPL owners. It will feature all of South Africa's top players, as well as a host of international talent such as Jos Butler, Liam Livingston, Jason Holder and Moeen Ali.

CSA hopes that the tournament will secure South African cricket's financial future, as well as provide a nursery to nurture the next generation of Proteas stars. A player auction held in September saw the likes of upcoming Proteas batsman Tristan Stubbs sold to the Eastern Cape Sunrisers for an eye-watering R9.2 million for the 21-year old.

With so much hope being placed on the SA20 as the panacea to cure the woes of South African cricket, what happens if it fails?

Press Release:


Another year, another debacle for South African cricket. After a promising win against India, defeat to Pakistan and then – of all countries – The Netherlands sent the Protea’s crashing out
of the T20 World Cup in Adelaide. It’s the latest in a series of painful exits from the 50 and 20 over global showdown since re-admission in 1992. Always full of promise, the Proteas have consistently failed to deliver – the much-maligned "chokers" tag weighing
ever more heavily. Years of maladministration, with hundreds of millions of rands in losses, have left the game in an existential crisis at a time when the very nature of world cricket is changing, and cricket boards are all turning to domestic T20 leagues
for financial salvation. How does South African cricket pick itself up and move forward in a time of upheaval for the world game?

Script:


ALL CHOKED-UP SCRIPT

V/O: South African Cricket and The World Cup – a doomed love affair

OPENING LINK: After another humbling defeat at a World Cup, this time to the lowly Netherlands, the tag of “Chokers” has never weighed so heavily around the next of the Proteas. It’s left South African cricket fans wondering if our team will ever be able to win a World Cup.

Graeme Smith: [00:03:53] I think South African fans have been disillusioned for a while, there's a lot of stuff that's been going on in South African cricket.

V/O: For Proteas legend and former CSA Director of Cricket Graeme Smith, the loss remains inexplicable.

Graeme Smith: [00:01:10] I found myself trying to justify why we should have batted better, you know, and then you realise that we lost the Holland, that there shouldn't be a justification for that.

V/O: In the wake of defeat, arguably South Africa’s greatest Captain knows how difficult post-tournament press conferences can be.

Graeme Smith: [00:02:07] There's no excuses to be made, really. And often these types of press conferences, you know, people want answers. But effectively, as a leader, you've got to take a lot on the chin and you've got to take a lot of responsibility.

V/O: It’s a task current leader Temba Bavuma must now confront

Temba Bavuma: [00:07:10] I think I'm still trying to process it all. You have to accept to have to accept that, you know, we're going to carry that tag again. The Chokers tag.

Aslam Khota: [00:02:52] I felt for him because here was a man woefully out of form. He had very little match practice given the number of injuries and illnesses he had running up to the tournament.

V/O: So where to now for the Proteas? Respected commentator Alsam Khota expects a thorough review

Aslam Khota: [00:06:12] Well, it's going to it's going to be a long, hard ask internally as individuals. Some of those who are responsible for those decisions, whether it was even at administrative level or down to the playing squads that went across. The only thing you need to do now is the drawing board.

V/O: The Protea's struggles on the field have been exacerbated by chaos in the boardrooms of Cricket South Africa. Years of maladministration have taken their toll and driven cricket to the verge of bankruptcy

Aslam Khota: [00:07:49] Most crises stem out of maladministration, lack of finance and. Cricket South Africa have had both of it. finance is still a massive issue. [00:08:05][16.0]

V/O: It comes at a time of rapid change for cricket worldwide thanks to the rise of domestic 20-over cricket that has injected huge money into the game.

Graeme Smith: [00:05:01] Now most of the top nations have their own sort of 20-over tournament. And I think both on the back of the success of the IPL, you've seen the Big Bash, the UK started the hundred and it was very important that South Africa was able to create something, something to be a sustainable part of its future

V/O: CSA has tried twice to create a domestic T20 league. First in 2017 with the Global T20 - which failed to attract a broadcast partner and was cancelled before a ball was bowled. Then came the loss-making Mzansi Super League which ran for 2 years, draining the already stretched coffers of CSA to breaking point.

Aslam Khota: [00:17:51] As one of the major cricketing nations for us to be starting this late in itself is something that needs to be corrected. It needs to happen. [00:18:05][14.4]

V/O: Now comes the SA20 – a brand new tournament featuring 6 franchises bankrolled by wealthy Indian owners. Scheduled to begin in January next year, the tournament is a top priority for CSA.

Graeme Smith: [00:12:13] They gave me a fancy name for the CEO but I've been at the coalface of building, SA20 right from the start. We believe that this is going to be that kind of a stand-out four to five weeks of cricket every year. We've attracted some of the best international talent. We’re hoping to elevate 60 or 70 South Africans every year onto the global stage and we hope that in turn, that'll improve our cricket

V/O: The team names will have a familiar ring to IPL fans: The Joburg Super Kings, MI Cape Town, the Durban Super Giants, the Paarl Royals, the Sunrisers Eastern Cape and the Pretoria Capitals.

Graeme Smith: [00:06:32] we were able to attract you know, six of the biggest trading brands in the world, which is huge because, you know, not only is it the investments into South Africa, into South African cricket, but they have the ability to sustain and to build with you

V/O: After years of struggle, CSA is betting that the SA20 could provide desperately needed financial stability.y Chief Marketing Officer Wanele Mngomezulu says this is crucial

Wanele Mngomezulu: [00:35:38] We've got an ailing cricket product which is CSA that desperately needs funds, that destiny needs to be financially sustainable. Yes, I think it's all known that this is a third try. Uh, yes. The first one, I think it all centres around the broadcast rights.

V/O: Locally the SA20 has secured Supersport as host broadcaster but crucially an international partner has also been found, in a deal that will infuse hundreds of millions of Rands into South African cricket.

Wanele Mngomezulu: [00:43:49] so now the feed will go to the Indian community, almost a billion fans

Graeme Smith: [00:09:59] to be able to do a standalone broadcast deal out of India for a league is almost unheard of. commercially it is important. Cricket South Africa has had financial stresses over the last number of years. So to attract these types of investments as well, we hope to commercially strengthen cricket in this country. [00:10:36][36.3]

V/O: Each team features a roster of 17 made up of top local and overseas players. The squads were chosen at the inaugural SA20 Player Auction from a pool of 300 potentials. These included all the Proteas, upcoming homegrown talent, and a host of international stars

Graeme Smith: [00:15:49] This is the first time I think an auction of that level has been done before in South Africa, we really wanted to deliver it at a level that would make our partners proud. You know, they've been involved in IPL auctions for years now [00:16:03][14.5]

V/O: A staggering R125 million was spent on players at the auction, with young Proteas batsman Tristan Stubbs the most expensive of the night, bought for R9.2million by the Sunrisers

Graeme Smith: [00:16:17] I think the amount of money that got pumped into player salaries is incredible, you know? And I think the advantages it keeps of top players in our game invested into South African cricket. [00:16:34][16.8]
V/O: But while the tournament may solve the financial woes of CSA, will it change the fortunes of the national team? Worryingly, National Captain Temba Bavuma went unsold.

​​Graeme Smith: [00:17:34] I feel for Temba. But, you know, it's it's having been a part of auctions myself. They're crazy places, you know, and some people do really well and some don't, unfortunately.

V/O: Then there’s next year’s Cricket World Cup to consider… and surprisingly CSA have chosen the SA20 over automatic qualification by deciding to forfeit an ODI series against Australia that was scheduled for the same time

Wanele Mngomezulu: [00:22:10] I understand from a fan perspective to say the game has to be at the forefront, but as an organisation we have to prioritise SA20 in terms of ensuring that we can fund our World Cup initiatives
So we intentionally made the decision to forego the Australia ODI and we fully understand and appreciate the impact that it has on us qualifying for the World Cup [00:20:31][11.4]

V/O: In the wake of another painful World Cup exit, South African cricket stands at a crossroads. A painful post-mortem awaits. They return home, a team diminished, facing an uncertain future in both Test match and white-ball cricket. While the SA20 looks like a step in the right direction, will it be the panacea to cure the woes of South African cricket?

PROMOS
PROMO 1: Up-sound of Proteas defeated by Netherlands.

After so many painful exits from ICC World Cups, defeat to the Netherlands surely ranks as the most disappointing of all.

What will it take for the Proteas to shed the tag of “Chokers” once and for all?


PROMO 2: Up-sound of Proteas defeated by Netherlands.

Another world cup, another painful Proteas exit.

Up-sound of SA20 Promo: That is huge! That is Huge! Cracked that as well!

Will the upcoming SA20, be the magic bullet to revitalise South African cricket and take us back to the top of the world?


PROMO 3: The newly launched SA20 has ambitions to become the most popular domestic T20 league after the IPL. But will fans disillusioned by the state of South African cricket flock to support a tournament that’s supposed to breathe new life into game in this country?

And I think the advantages it keeps of top players in our game invested into South African cricket. [00:16:34][16.8] V/O: But while the tournament may solve the financial woes of CSA, will it change the fortunes of the national team? Worryingly, National Captain Temba Bavuma went unsold. ​​Graeme Smith: [00:17:34] I feel for Temba. But, you know, it's it's having been a part of auctions myself. They're crazy places, you know, and some people do really well and some don't, unfortunately. V/O: Then there’s next year’s Cricket World Cup to consider… and surprisingly CSA have chosen the SA20 over automatic qualification by deciding to forfeit an ODI series against Australia that was scheduled for the same time Wanele Mngomezulu: [00:22:10] I understand from a fan perspective to say the game has to be at the forefront, but as an organisation we have to prioritise SA20 in terms of ensuring that we can fund our World Cup initiatives So we intentionally made the decision to forego the Australia ODI and we fully understand and appreciate the impact that it has on us qualifying for the World Cup [00:20:31][11.4] V/O: In the wake of another painful World Cup exit, South African cricket stands at a crossroads. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): In the wake of yet another World Cup debacle, how will the Proteas pick up the pieces and shed that eternal tag of Chokers?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: In the wake of a shock defeat to the Netherlands that dumped South Africa out of the T20 World Cup in Australia, we find out what's next for the shell-shocked Proteas and how South African cricket plans to move forward from yet another World Cup debacle.
metadata.Summary: Since 1992, South Africa has endured many-a-painful exit from both the 50 over and T20 world Cups. Always full of promise, the Proteas have consistently flattered to deceive, earning the much-maligned "chokers" tag that they carry with ever-increasing weight around their necks. Now in the wake of Sunday's shock loss to the lowly Netherlands, Temba Bavuma is the latest Captain to bear the burden of defeat. They return home with cricket in a state of flux. After years of maladministration that has seen hundreds of millions of rands in losses, the game in this country faces an existential threat. It comes at a time in which the very nature of world cricket is changing. As interest in bilateral series wanes, cricket boards from around the world are all turning to Domestic T20 leagues for financial salvation.
metadata.Further information: India has the IPL, Australia the Big Bash, England the Hundred. And in January, South Africa will have the SA20. This much-heralded T20 competition is the latest attempt by CSA to launch a successful domestic T20 league. Previous attempts have been unmitigated financial disasters. The Global T20 envisioned by former CEO Haroon Lorgat was canceled at the last minute, but not before CSA had invested millions into it. Its successor, the Mzansi Super League ran for 2 years, but failure to secure a broadcast sponsor resulted crippled it financially. Headed by Commissioner Graeme Smith, the SA20 was launched in August. Scheduled for January and February 2023, the tournament will be played between 6 newly-formed franchises bankrolled by wealthy IPL owners. It will feature all of South Africa's top players, as well as a host of international talent such as Jos Butler, Liam Livingston, Jason Holder and Moeen Ali. CSA hopes that the tournament will secure South African cricket's financial future, as well as provide a nursery to nurture the next generation of Proteas stars. A player auction held in September saw the likes of upcoming Proteas batsman Tristan Stubbs sold to the Eastern Cape Sunrisers for an eye-watering R9.2 million for the 21-year old. With so much hope being placed on the SA20 as the panacea to cure the woes of South African cricket, what happens if it fails?
